title: Artificial Intelligence + Robots Reconstruct Parking Space and Solve Urban Parking Problems
summary: Shanghai AI Research Institute says that AI-assisted robotic parking runs in operating garages and estimates that single-layer layouts can raise capacity by 60–80%.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Shanghai AI Research Institute describes AI-assisted robotic parking in operating garages, with further projects under construction. Perception, planning and scheduling coordinate vehicle storage and retrieval. The institute estimates that single-layer layouts can increase capacity by 60–80%. It gives a second estimate in the same account: An ordinary lot of about 100 spaces can be converted within one month and can then gain about 50% more spaces, with an annual return on investment that can reach 30%. The institute names no garage where either figure was measured. It describes easier parking and retrieval in qualitative terms only. No source measures a change in waiting time.
purpose: Increase parking capacity and simplify vehicle storage and retrieval.
system: AI robotic parking and scheduling system
developer: Shangyuan Lijiao (Shanghai) Technology Co., Ltd. (上元立交（上海）科技有限公司)

ratings.reason: The institute states that capacity 'can reach' 60–80% more with a single-layer layout and about 50% more for a lot of about 100 spaces. Both are conditional estimates, and no garage reports a realized gain.
The institute describes easier parking and vehicle retrieval in garages that already use the system. The claim is qualitative, and no source measures a change in waiting time.

ai_role.statement: AI perception and planning are described as components of a robotic parking system. Garage geometry, vehicle-handling hardware and scheduling also contribute to capacity; the 60–80% figure is stated potential.

data.answer:
Shanghai AI Research Institute describes robotic parking deployments and says that single-layer layouts can increase capacity by 60–80%. The percentage is potential, not a measured outcome.

The 60–80%, over-110%, and roughly-50% capacity figures describe different configurations or general renovation scenarios and should not be combined. The 30% annual return is also an unsupported estimate here. No site-level waiting-time, cost, safety, or occupancy evaluation establishes the net benefit.
